507	The instance parameter grid has no second Region Type field: the Type Selector is the type control. Non-masking regions
508	replace model backgrounds while retaining visible cut outlines, cut foreground patterns (including solid foregrounds),
509	and projected model lines. `render/regions.rs` finds the drawing's ink once (the model layer's lines and patterns, less what a
510	later fill covers, so a low wall hidden by a cut wall does not reappear; and a section's or elevation's hidden-line picture as
511	runs of its pixels, which is all the ink an elevation has) and gives each region the part of it in its area: the outline less
512	its holes, inside an odd number of rings, less the masking regions drawn before it. A line is kept where it lies in the area or
513	within half its stroke of it (its pen's width as it will draw, from the owner's object style while the pen is not set yet), so a
514	region edge sketched on a wall face keeps the whole face; Visibility/Graphics weights wider than the object style's are not
515	allowed for. Lines are cut by the rings and the masks as they are, never by boolean operations on polygons (which are cubic in
516	the corners an outline can have): only the model's filled patterns are, by the pieces of the area they reach. The pieces of a
517	polyline that meet stay one line, so its corners keep their joins, and a dashed line's dashes stay where they were (the dashes of
518	the cycle a piece begins in are solid lines of their own). A section's ink belongs to the region that keeps it (`Part::Pattern`),
519	so a sheet's viewport, which keeps what an element owns, has it. A caller that has the section's picture (the desktop's, a sheet's,
520	`section_png`'s) hands it in (`render::section_over`, `section_at_over`), at the view's size or a multiple of it (a screen with more
521	pixels to the point), and the ink is the picture's own pixels, as runs: a row of a pixel's height, and a run of up to two pixels
522	that sits on one of the row above (the edge of a tall wall) joined to it as one vertical line, so 200 walls 20 m tall at 4000 x 2600
523	px are some hundreds of lines and not a million runs. A picture of more than 250,000 runs (noise, not drawings) keeps the first
524	250,000 and the drawing's `notes` say the ink of the last rows is under the region. `render::section` draws a picture of its own
525	when a non-masking region wants one, which costs what the picture does, every call. Masking still hides the model; detail annotation remains above the
526	region. The same display list feeds the desktop, PNG, SVG and sheet viewports.
527	
528	Limits, kept as Revit has them or not yet built: a non-masking region with a solid background hides a room's tag text while its outlines
529	stay (Revit keeps room tags above filled regions: not verified); grids, levels and room fills are drawn before the regions, so a masking
530	region hides them; there is no Bring to Front or Send to Back, a region is over the model and under the annotation, in the order of its
531	id; Move and Rotate carry a region's or a floor's model pattern with it (`pattern_origin`), where Revit may leave a model pattern fixed in
532	the building, and Align moves it; a filled region drawn on a sheet itself is plain annotation over the viewports, so a solid one hides
533	what lies under it (Revit has no regions on sheets).
534	
535	Sketch snapping (`snap::in_sketch`) combines the visible model's wall faces and slab edges, detail lines and existing
536	region boundaries in the active view, and the draft's own lines. It supports endpoints, midpoints (of each segment of a
537	polyline), intersections (where two walls meet is one too), perpendiculars, nearest points and angle guides, the anchors of
538	annotation (a note's insertion point and leader, a tag's head, a dimension's stations, a spot elevation, section and elevation
539	marks, detail groups and repeating details), and a camera's eye and target rather than its mark's body or name, honoring Manage > Snaps
540	and one-point overrides. An element being edited is omitted as a model snap target; its draft supplies the boundary instead.
541	Rectangle and arc previews use the same origin points and Shift constraint as a click. Annotation in another independent view,
542	or hidden by Visibility/Graphics, is excluded. A plan view cuts where its own view range says (`plan_range` of the view, not of its
543	level); a section or an elevation has no plan to snap to, only its own detail lines and regions. Of what the plan builds, the
544	nearest `MAX_OUTLINES` elements within reach have their outlines snapped to (one `walls::Index` for them all), and the nearest
545	`MAX_NEAR` chords are tried against each other. Ceilings snap in a floor plan as well as a ceiling plan, because a snap does not know
546	which of the two the cursor is in, and the members of a detail group are not snap targets.
547	
548	The reference workflows are Autodesk's [fill layers](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/Revit-GetStarted/files/GUID-8A38ADC8-98A6-4A30-BD21-1886F044F6ED.htm),
549	[region editing](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/Revit-DocumentPresent/files/GUID-183D9B1E-6554-4C19-9EA9-B32C8D2A5C9D.htm),
550	and [sketch snaps](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/Revit-Customize/files/GUID-A3947840-1F30-41D7-AF75-B61687952A07.htm).
551	Boundary weights follow each boundary line's style. See also Autodesk's [region masking behavior](https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Filled-Region-with-solid-fill-does-not-cover-all-elements-in-Revit.html).
552	
553	A material's cut and surface may be one of the project's fill patterns (`Material::cut_pattern`, `surface_pattern`, a
554	library reference like a region type's), over the patterns drawn in code (`model::Pattern`), which stay for the materials
555	that name them: `material` takes either name for `cut` and `surface`, and the desktop's material editor lists both. A fill
556	pattern a material shows can't be deleted, and is renamed with it. `render::fill_pattern` draws a fill pattern for a
557	region, a cut layer (its courses along the layer) and a floor's or a ceiling's surface. A model pattern is aligned and
558	rotated as Revit's: a filled region and a floor hold `pattern_origin` and `pattern_angle` (`fills::strokes_placed`), which
559	Move, Rotate and Mirror carry with the element; Align with a pattern line picked second (`render::pattern_line_at`) moves the
560	origin so that line lies on the reference, and Properties shows Pattern Angle. `Model::align_pattern(id, reference, line)` is
561	that arithmetic (the origin moved across by the gap between the two parallel lines, to the micron; the error says when the
562	element has no model pattern, or the lines aren't parallel or have no length), so every front end gets the same answer and
563	sets it with `modify`. `pattern_origin` and `pattern_angle` are in the `modify`, `filled_region` and `floor` command docs, and
564	`elements` shows them for a region and a floor even at their defaults.
565	
566	## Linked models
567	
568	A `Link` element (`link.rs`; commands `link` and `reload`) is another project shown in this one as a reference. The file holds its name, its
569	path, where its origin stands (`at`) and a turn (`angle`); what it read is `Model::loaded`, by path, outside the file (`serde(skip)`), filled by
570	`link`, `reload` and `open` (`relink`, which doesn't follow the links of a linked file). The views draw `link::seen(model)`: the project with
571	each loaded link's built elements (`built`: not its views, sheets, annotation, detail lines, filled regions, detail groups, rooms, grids or links) moved and turned by `commands::transformed`
572	and brought in with `insert::insert_as(.., linked: true)` under ids from `LINKED` up (`ids.rs`), so `link::is_linked(id)` tells them; a level of the
573	link at the height of one of the project's (1 mm) is that level, another comes in named `link: level`. Everything that takes a `&Model` draws and snaps to
574	them without knowing: `Look::with` makes a linked id halftone, and picking never answers one (`Drawing::pick_all`, `in_box`, `Image::pick`,
575	`in_box`, `shows` and `Mesh::pick` leave them out). The commands that make an image (`render`, `save` to svg, png or pdf) draw `seen`; the desktop's
576	`view_model` does, cached by the project's `Arc`. The schedules, `Model::check`, IFC and every command that edits work on the project itself.
577	To do: shared coordinates, a link's graphics overrides and visibility per view, hosting on a linked wall, unloading.
578	
579	## Dimensions
580	
581	A dimension (`Dimension`, the `dimension` command) measures the model as it is, so it follows what it measures. Its `refs` are lines
582	(`Reference {id, face}`: a wall's centre line, faces and ends, a door's or window's centre and jambs, a grid, a straight detail line) or, with
583	`point: start|end`, the point at that end of one (`Model::reference_point`: a wall's centre line ends where its location line does, a face where
584	the outline turns off it, so at the mitred corner; a detail line of any shape at its ends; `reference_points` lists them, `endpoint_at` finds the
585	nearest, `{endpoint: [x, y]}` in a command). `reference_geometry` gives either as a line, a point as a line of no length, and `crossings` lays
586	them along the way the dimension measures (`measured_along`): a linear one's `orient` (horizontal or vertical), else square to its first line,
587	else from its first point to the next elsewhere. `Model::check` refuses a line not parallel to the first, or not square to a linear one's line,
588	and points all in one place. Mirror keeps the end of a line along the element and flips the one across it (`Reference::mirrored`); Flip swaps
589	both. A linear one given no `orient` runs vertical where `at` is east or west of everything it measures, else horizontal; the desktop's Auto
590	(`dims::Placing::kind`) also lays an aligned one where the cursor is among the points (`Orient::follow`), as Archicad does. Radial and diameter
591	dimensions measure round columns, curved walls (centre line or a face) and circles and arcs (`reference_arc`); arc length, a curved wall's or an
592	arc's length along it (`reference_sweep`), all of it or, with two point references after the arc, between them (`Model::arc_span`), its line an arc through `at` round the same centre. `dims::round_at` picks the face nearest a click.
593	
594	Each dimension has a dimension type (`dims.rs`, `Model::dimension_types`, a library entry `Kind::DimensionType`, the `dimension_type` command),
595	Revit's type parameters with lengths in mm on paper: Dimension String Type (continuous, baseline, ordinate), tick mark (diagonal, arrow, open
596	arrow, dot, none) and its size, line and tick pens, colour, dimension line extension, Witness Line Control (gap to element, or fixed to the
597	dimension line with its length), witness line gap and extension, baseline spacing, centre marks, and its text: font (as text types take one,
598	`DimensionType::lettering`), size, bold, italic, underline, width factor, offset, opaque or transparent background, Read Convention, units and
599	rounding (`DimensionType::length`), and the radius and diameter symbols and the equality text. A project starts with `Diagonal - 2.5mm Arial`,
600	which aligned, linear, angular and arc length dimensions start in, and `Arrow - 2.5mm Arial`, which radial and diameter ones do
601	(`dims::default_type`); a file of format 9 gives its dimensions their kind's (`Model::typed_dimensions`). A dimension's own text, Revit's
602	instance values, is a prefix, a suffix, text above and below, Replace With Text and Equality Display, and a segment may have its own over it
603	(`texts`, `SegmentText`, the `dimension_text` command; `Dimension::text` reads one through the other, `dimension_segment_at` finds a segment by a
604	point); `Model::dimension_labels` is what its
605	numbers read (and `elements` shows as `labels`): a baseline string's each from its first reference, an ordinate's each witness line's, the first 0.
606	An aligned or linear dimension may be kept equal (`equal`, Revit's EQ, which also turns its Equality Display on) and have segments
607	locked at a length (`locked`, `Lock`; the `dimension_constraint` command). `constraints::keep` runs in `Session::execute` after every undoable
608	command, before the check: each constrained dimension is solved on its own line (its `stations`, each with its reference), a locked segment tying
609	two stations rigidly and equality tying all its segments to one length (a locked one's, else its ends', which stay where they are, so an inner
610	reference dragged goes back); a run of tied stations stays where what the command moved puts it, else where its first is. What has to move is
611	moved by `commands::move_by`, as `move` moves it, and the dimensions are solved again (`PASSES`) until all hold; where they can't (locked
612	lengths that differ made equal, one element pulled two ways), the command is refused, saying which dimension, and nothing changes.
613	A length typed for a segment (`dimension_value`; in the window, a click on the selected dimension's number, as a temporary
614	dimension's takes one) moves what the segment ends at, its second station's reference, along the dimension by the difference
615	(`move_by`), and a locked segment is locked at it; the other locks then hold or the command is refused. Align with `lock` (Revit's
616	padlock: in the window, the open padlock Align offers on the line it moved) leaves a lock: a dimension of the aligned line's reference
617	and the reference's (`to`, else whatever has a line along it), its one segment locked at 0 and `alignment` set, which
618	`constraints::keep` holds as it holds the others, so the two lines stay on one line whatever either is moved by; one that can't hold
619	with the other locks is refused, and the project is as it was. A lock is drawn by a front end, never on paper (`render/dimensions.rs`
620	draws nothing of it): the window shows each locked segment's shut padlock whether its dimension is selected or not, and each alignment
621	lock's padlock beside where its lines meet, which a click unlocks (deletes). Format 15 holds them; 14 would read one as a dimension of
622	nothing.
623	`render/dimensions.rs` draws them all as the type says (`Ink`: its lines, ticks and witness lines, and its numbers laid out by `crate::text`
624	over the paper where the background is opaque).
625	
626	A 3D view has dimensions of its own (`Element::Dimension3D`, the `dimension_3d` command; `dims3d.rs`), as Revit's aligned dimension in a 3D
627	view: two references (`Ref3`), each a point of the model or a point on an edge (its two ends with it), and a point its line passes through,
628	kept by the view (`view`, a GUID: deleting the view takes them with it) and of a dimension type as a plan's are. Between two points it measures
629	straight from one to the other; to an edge, square to the edge's line, so between two parallel edges it is how far apart they are
630	(`dims3d::ends`). They hold places in space, not references to elements: moving an element leaves them, and `move`, `rotate` and `mirror`
631	take them in plan when they are moved themselves. They draw as marks (`dims3d::marks`, `Mark`: a polyline in the picture's pixels, its width
632	and colour), through any camera and at any paper size (`SCREEN` pixels a paper millimetre on screen, `sheet::DENSITY` on a sheet): a
633	witness line from each end of what it measures to its line, its line, a tick at each end and its number lettered along it in our strokes
634	(`font.rs`), reading from the left, on the side away from what it measures; nothing hides them. `dims3d::paint` paints marks into the
635	processor's picture, which the `render` command does for a 3D view; a sheet draws them as its own lines over the view's picture, so they print
636	in its PDF; the window draws them over the picture on either painter (the card's too) with the theme's ink, the selection's colour when
637	picked. Visibility/Graphics hides them with Dimensions (`category_of`). In the window the Aligned Dimension tool (DI) in the 3D view picks a
638	corner seen within the snap's reach (`Scene::corner_near`), else an edge within a pick's (`Scene::edge_near`, the point of it nearest the
639	cursor), else the point of the face there; after two, a click places the line where it meets the plane through the two that faces the
640	camera most (`dims3d::line_through`), and the status line says how long it is. In Modify a click on a dimension's lines picks it before what
641	the picture shows under them (`dims3d::pick`).
642

//! A session: the project, its file, and its undo history; commands run here.

use crate::json::Value;
use crate::project::Project;

pub struct Step {
    pub before: Project,
    pub after: Project,
    pub label: String,
}

pub struct Session {
    pub project: Project,
    pub path: Option<String>,
    pub undo: Vec<Step>,
    pub redo: Vec<Step>,
    pub read_only: bool,
    /// The phase and design option this session makes elements in.
    pub now_phase: Option<String>,
    pub now_option: Option<String>,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the original and my build with the same args in fresh dirs; diff normalized outputs.
usage: cmp.py [-q] [-f file_to_copy]... -- args...
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, difflib
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
GUID = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r'"uid": \d+', '"uid": <UID>', s)
    m = {}
    def rep(mo):
        g = mo.group(0)
        if g not in m: m[g] = 'GUID-%d' % (len(m)+1)
        return m[g]
    s = GUID.sub(rep, s)
    s = re.sub(r"\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]{6}", ".tmpXXXXXX", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    # IFC GlobalIds
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm)+1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    return s
def run(exe, args, files, stdin):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cmp')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    before = set(os.listdir(d))
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, input=stdin, timeout=120)
    out = {'stdout': p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'stderr': p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'code': p.returncode}
    fl = {}
    for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, d)
            if rel in before: 
                pass
            try: fl[rel] = open(full,'rb').read()
            except Exception as e: fl[rel] = b'<unreadable>'
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out, fl
def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    quiet = False; files = []; stdin = None
    while a and a[0] != '--':
        if a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-i': stdin = open(a[1],'rb').read(); a = a[2:]
        else: break
    if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
    o, of = run(ORIG, a, files, stdin)
    m, mf = run(MINE, a, files, stdin)
    ok = True
    for k in ('code', 'stdout', 'stderr'):
        x = norm(str(o[k])); y = norm(str(m[k]))
        if x != y:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- {k} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x.splitlines(), y.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:40]:
                print(l[:300])
    for f in sorted(set(of) | set(mf)):
        if f not in of: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in mine'); continue
        if f not in mf: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in orig'); continue
        x, y = of[f], mf[f]
        try:
            xs = norm(x.decode('utf-8')); ys = norm(y.decode('utf-8'))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            if x != y: ok = False; print(f'--- binary file {f} differs ({len(x)} vs {len(y)} bytes)')
            continue
        if xs != ys:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- file {f} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(xs.splitlines(), ys.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:60]:
                print(l[:300])
    print('SAME' if ok else 'DIFF')
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
main()

| Visibility and graphics | What each view hides, and how it draws the rest, as Revit's Visibility/Graphics does, for each plan, section, elevation and 3D view: whole categories left out (walls, doors, rooms, grids, dimensions, levels in a section…), or single elements; lines and fills overridden by category, by element and by view filter: a colour, weight and dash for what the view cuts and for what it sees (a plan's below its cut plane, the annotation; in 3D, and in a section beyond its line, the edges' colour), the cut's poché colour or a 3D view's surface colour (a weight is a pen, 0 a hairline at any scale), halftone (halfway to the paper) and, in 3D, transparency, where what lies behind shows through and a click still picks the element (halftone and transparency only add: a filter or an element can't take its category's away). A hidden door or window leaves its opening in the wall, and snaps, Tag All, Select All and a view's framing take what it shows. View filters pick elements out by rules, a schedule filter's (a field of the category, how to compare it, a value, project parameters among the fields), on the categories chosen; a view applies them in order, the first prevailing where they disagree, and one that hides hides whatever the others say; an element's own override beats the filters', and those beat the category's. View templates keep a view's categories, filters, phase, design options, scale, detail level, visual style and, for a plan, view range under a name, for other views to follow: what a template controls isn't the view's to change, and changed, every view following it follows. A project's filters and templates are saved with it; sheets print each view as its graphics say |
| Visibility/Graphics | View > Visibility/Graphics (VV, VG) opens the active view's dialog, a table as Revit's: a row for each model category (searched by name, with All, None and Invert, and Object Styles… for what isn't overridden), its visibility, then Projection/Surface Lines, Patterns and Transparency, Cut Lines and Patterns, each cell showing what it overrides (the line as it draws, the fill's colour, the percent) and opening its own small dialog (lines: a colour, weight and dash, each with a box that turns it on; patterns: a fill colour; transparency, seen in 3D; Clear Overrides), Halftone a box in the row, and Detail Level, By View until a category can have its own; the Annotation Categories have their lines and halftone; Filters applies the project's filters in order, each a row alike, with Add, Remove, Up and Down; Elements lists what's hidden or overridden one by one. Design Options picks which option of each set the view shows (the primary unless it chooses). OK and Apply send what changed as one `graphics` command, one undo step; Cancel drops it. A view that follows a view template shows what the template controls, and leaves it be |
| Hide in View | Select, then Modify > View: Hide Element (EH) leaves the elements out of the view, Hide Category (VH) every category the selection is of, Override Graphics (EO) opens Visibility/Graphics on its Elements tab with the selection added. Unhide Elements (EU) opens that tab, with what's hidden; tick a box to bring it back |
| Scale, detail level, visual style | The view control bar's first buttons. In a plan, a section or an elevation, Scale lists 1 : 1 to 1 : 1000, or in a project in feet and inches the architect's scales (12" = 1'-0" to 1/32" = 1'-0") and the engineer's (1" = 10'-0" to 1" = 200'-0"), and takes any other typed in Custom, as n, 1 : n or `1/4" = 1'-0"` (every view has one: 1 : 100, or 1/8" = 1'-0" in feet and inches, until it is given another, and its annotation and line weights are the paper's at that scale); Detail Level picks Coarse, Medium or Fine. In the 3D view, Visual Style picks Shaded, Hidden Line or Wireframe; WF, HL and SD do too, as in Revit. Its menu ends with Graphic Display Options (GD, as Revit's): Show Edges, Silhouettes (none, or an outline 1 to 10 px wide round what stands against what is behind) and Show Ambient Shadows (soft shadows where faces meet), drawn alike on the processor and on the graphics card. Each is one undo step, saved with the project, and in a sheet's viewport the view draws as it says. A view's Properties have the same: View Scale (the scales the Scale menu lists), Scale Value 1: (a typed scale) and Detail Level, or in the 3D view Visual Style. A view that follows a view template that controls one shows the template's value, greyed out, with the template's name on hover |
| Filters, view templates | View > Filters (FT): New makes a view filter; tick its categories and add rules as a schedule's filter has them. View > View Templates (VT), as Revit's: the templates on the left, on a tab for each kind of view (Plan, Elevation/Section, 3D), with New from This View (a template of the view open), Duplicate, Rename and Delete under them; on the right the one picked, a table of Parameter, Value and Include: its view scale, detail level and visual style, its V/G Overrides, V/G Filters and Design Options (Visibility/Graphics on the template), its view range, phase and phase filter, its background grids, each ticked under Include for the views following it to take. OK and Apply send each template's changes as one command; Cancel drops them. A view's Properties name its template on a button that opens the same dialog, <None> first, to pick the one it follows |
| `purge` | PU | `kinds?` (`type`, `family`, `material`, `picture`, `filter`, `template`; types and families by default), `dry_run?`: takes out what nothing uses, again for what that frees; a category keeps a type and a family a type; `dry_run` lists what would go |
| `scale` | | `view?`, `scale?` (the n of 1 : n, 1 to 100000; 1 : 100, or 1 : 96 in feet and inches, until set): a plan's, section's or elevation's scale, the paper it stands for, which sizes its annotation and its line weights; a viewport placed with no `scale` takes it; without `scale`, what the view has |
| `detail` | | `view?`, `detail?` (`coarse`, `medium` or `fine`): how much a plan, a section or an elevation draws of what it cuts; without `detail`, what the view has |
| `visual_style` | | `view?` (`{3D}`), `style?` (`shaded`, `hidden_line` or `wireframe`): how a 3D view draws its surfaces; the default 3D view comes to be as it is first changed; without `style`, what the view has |
| `graphic_display_options` | GD | `view?` (`{3D}`), `edges?`, `silhouette?` (px, 0 to 10), `ambient_shadows?`: Revit's Graphic Display Options for a 3D view: its edges on or off in Shaded, a silhouette that wide round what stands against what is behind, soft shadows where faces meet; what is left out stays; with none, what the view has |
| `graphics` | | `view?` (a level's, section's or elevation's name or id, or `{3D}`), `hide?` and `show?` ([categories]: walls, rooms, grids, levels…), `hide_elements?` and `show_elements?` ([ids]), `categories?` and `elements?` ({category or id: override}; an override is {`hidden?`, `projection?` and `cut?` ({`color?`, `weight?` (a pen: 0 a hairline at any scale, 1 to 16 from 0.10 to 2 mm on paper at 1 : 100), `dash?` (`solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`), `fill?`}), `halftone?`, `transparency?` (percent, seen in 3D)}, merged into the last, null takes it away), `filters?` ([{`filter`, plus an override's fields}, …], the first prevailing), `template?` (a view template's name, or null), `phase?` and `phase_filter?` (names, or null), `options?` ({set: option, null takes the choice away}), `reset?`: what a view hides and how it draws the rest; none of them: the view's settings as they are |
| `filter` | | `name`, `categories?` (any a schedule can be of), `rules?` ([{`field`, `op`, `value`}, …] as a schedule's `filters`), `delete?`: a view filter, and the ids it picks out; a view applies it with `graphics` |
| `template` | | `name`, `from?` (a view to take the categories, filters, a plan's view range, scale, detail level and visual style from, and its kind), `like?` (a template to copy), `kind?` (`plan`, `section`, `3d`, null for any), `rename?`, `controls?` ([`categories`, `filters`, `range`, `phase`, `options`, `scale`, `detail`, `style`]), `view_range?`, `scale?`, `detail?`, `visual_style?`, the changes `graphics` makes to a view's categories, filters, phase and options, `delete?`: a view template, for views to follow with `graphics {template}`; a view that follows one that controls the scale, the detail level or the visual style can't set it (`scale`, `detail` and `visual_style` refuse) |

content.content:
and edits, the selection staying as it is: `BimApp::palette_ids` is the selection narrowed to it, and the palette's subject, the Type
Selector, Edit Type (from the palette, the ribbon or the right-click menu) and every edit the palette sends read it, never the selection.
`palette_filter` keeps the selection it was picked for, so a new selection starts it over.

View Templates (`templates.rs`). VT and View > View Templates open it as Revit's does, in the look Type Properties has: on the left a tab for each
kind of view (`ViewKind`: Plan, Elevation/Section, 3D; a template of no kind is on every tab), the templates of the one showing, and Duplicate…,
Rename… and Delete, with New from This View… (enabled on the tab of the active view's kind) under them, each opening a Name row; they run at once
(`template` with `like`, `rename`, `delete`, `from`). On the right the template picked: a table of Parameter, Value and Include, its rows the groups
its kind holds (`ViewKind::groups`), each group's Include box named for the group. Its settings edit a draft (`TemplatesDialog::drafts`, one per
template, kept through Duplicate and Rename); OK and Apply send each template's difference as one `template` command, Cancel drops them.
V/G Overrides, V/G Filters and Design Options open Visibility/Graphics on the template's draft (`VgDialog::for_template`: no Elements tab nor a
drawing's layers, which are a view's own; its OK puts the categories, filters and options back in the draft), View Range a small dialog of
its four offsets, and Background Grids the grid editor. A view's Properties name its template on a button (`properties::wide_button`, as wide as the drop-downs, as Edit… is), which
opens the same dialog as Assign View Template: <None> first, the view's kind's tab showing, and OK also sets the template the view follows.

Visibility sets (`BimApp::visibility_sets`, `templates.rs`, the same in both profiles) are view templates, switched from the view control bar: no
Dimension Type Properties (`dimtypes.rs`), and Properties edits its prefix, suffix, text above and below, Replace With Text and Equality Display.
A double click on one of its numbers opens Dimension Text for that segment (`DimensionTextDialog`). Selected, an aligned or linear one shows
a padlock under each segment and, over a string of two or more, EQ past its end (`dimension_constraints`): a click locks or unlocks, or makes
it equal or not.

## Background grids

Each plan, section and elevation keeps its canvas grid in its `Graphics::background_grid`, saved with the project, copied
with independent view duplicates, and edited through the undoable `graphics` command. Reflected ceiling plans use their
plan key's graphics, like their scale and other view settings; dependent plans follow their parent's graphics.
The Graphics group in a view's instance properties has a Background Grids Edit… button. The grid menu beside Temporary
Hide/Isolate (the glasses) keeps Show grids, independent Main grid and Subgrid checkboxes, Grid snapping and Grid settings….
The editor uses a draft: Apply/OK save one undo step, Cancel discards unapplied changes. File > Settings has no grid page;
application settings files from the earlier global implementation no longer affect views.

View templates can control Background Grids as a group (`Group::BackgroundGrid`, JSON `background_grid`), for plans and
elevations and sections. New from This View copies the effective grid. View Templates has a Background Grids row whose Edit… opens
the grid editor on the template's draft (`open_template_background_grid`; its OK hands the grid back, the templates' OK sends it). Followers use the
template's values and gray out their instance Edit button, bottom menu grid settings and any open editor; removing template
control restores each view's own grid. The engine rejects bypasses through `graphics` and `modify` too.

`core::background_grid` owns the lattice geometry, shared by painting and snapping. Both lattices start at the fixed view
origin (0, 0), with one counter-clockwise rotation in degrees. Main spacing X/Y is entered in the project's actual units;
subgrid divisions X/Y divide that spacing independently. Each grid has its own colour and pen (0–16), with default colours [230,230,230] for main and [245,245,245] for subgrid,
following the project's line weights and the Thin Lines display toggle. Main lines take precedence over coincident subgrid lines.
Dense subgrids disappear below four screen pixels; main grids thin by whole multiples without moving the origin. Drawing
is bounded to 4096 lines. Section/elevation textures expose empty paper behind the model while retaining opaque model faces.
Grids are canvas aids; they do not create elements or appear in sheet/export drawings.

Grid snapping is a global application preference (`BimApp::grid_snapping`, saved as `Settings::grid_snapping`), available
in Manage > Snaps and the bottom grid menu. It is not part of view graphics or view templates: the checkbox stays editable
when a template controls the active view's grid, and changing it creates no project undo step. New/Open retain the setting.
It uses intersections of the active view's enabled subgrid, or main grid when the subgrid is disabled; with neither enabled,
there is nothing to snap to. Show grids only controls display: snapping can remain on while the grid is hidden. Object snaps, one-point snap overrides and Shift
constraints keep priority; grid snapping replaces the free-point fallback and automatic angle guides. Sections and
elevations snap annotation placement in their local horizontal/height coordinates. Model validation rejects invalid
spacing, divisions, pens or rotation, and commands roll back the whole edit.

input.description: Read specs for related commands

content.content:
import_cad : {path | cad, name?, level?, view?, at?: [x, y], position?, units?, scale?, angle?, layers?, colors?, link?} brings in a DXF drawing (`path`: an ASCII DXF of any version, or a DWG, which the desktop and the command line read as DXF) or places one the project holds again (`cad`, its name), as an element in every plan of `level`, or with `view` (a plan) in that view only. `units` of the drawing: auto (the default: what its file says, else mm), mm, cm, m, in or ft; or `scale`, mm to each of its units. `position`: center (the default: the middle of the drawing on `at`, the origin unless given) or origin (its origin on `at`); `angle` turns it about `at`, degrees. `layers`: visible (the default: those its file has on and thawed), all, or a list of those to show. `colors`: preserve (the default), invert or black. `link: true` remembers the file, so `reload_cad` and opening the project read it again. Returns its id, the drawing's name, its unit, entities and layers, its extents in the model, how many entities lie far from the rest (they're left out of its extents) and what was left out, with `notes` on what a DWG's read left out

cad_layers : {id, hide?: [layer, …], show?: [layer, …], view?} a CAD import's layers, each with its colour and linetype and whether it's shown; `hide` and `show` change which it shows in every view, or with `view` in that view only (its Visibility/Graphics, by the drawing's name)

show_mass : {view?, show?} hides the masses in a view if it shows them, shows them if it hides them (or as `show`, a yes or no, says): the `mass` category of `graphics {hide|show}`, in one step. The reply has `shown` and `hidden`, the categories the view hides. Revit's Show Mass has no default shortcut; MH is BIMCraft's

room : {point: [x,y], level?, name?, number?, top_level?, limit_offset?, base_offset?, frozen?} bounded by the walls and the room separation lines around the point (walls the level's `computation_height` cuts; separation lines whatever their height). Placed where nothing encloses it, or in a space another room has (two rooms can't share one; the first keeps it), it is placed unbounded, a 1000 mm square, and the reply has a `warning`. Its height is Revit's: from `base_offset` mm over its level (0) up to `limit_offset` mm over its upper limit `top_level` (null: Not Bounded, over its own level). Unless given, 300 mm under the level above (`top_level` that level, `limit_offset` -300), or with none above, not bounded and 2500 mm tall. `elements` gives its `unbounded_height` and `volume_m3`, its area times that height. `frozen` (a yes or no; also `modify {id, frozen}`) keeps the boundary the room has now: it keeps its size whatever the walls do, and the walls are never searched for it again, which saves time in a project of many rooms. Unfrozen, it follows the walls again. Only an enclosed room can be frozen

section : {start: [x,y], end: [x,y], depth?, name?} a section view along the line, looking to its left (drawn west to east, it looks north): it cuts the model at the line and sees `depth` mm past it, or everything

elevation : {facing?: north|south|east|west, at?: [x,y], start?, end?, depth?, name?} an elevation view of the building's side `facing` (North shows the north side, looking south), from 3 m out, or through `at`; with `at` alone, of the side it's on; with `start` and `end`, along that line, looking to its left; with none, the four not there yet

duplicate_view : {view, mode?: duplicate|detailing|dependent, name?} a new plan view of a plan's level (a level's own plan, or a plan view; sections, elevations, schedules, sheets and the 3D view aren't duplicated yet): `duplicate` (the default) has the same view range, crop and graphics and no annotation of its own; `detailing` copies the dimensions, tags, notes and spot elevations in it too, as its own; `dependent` follows its parent's view range, graphics, scale and detail (change those in the parent), has a crop of its own and shows its parent's annotation as well as its own. Named `name`, else `<view> Copy 1` (`<view> Dependent 1`). Commands that take a level or a view take it by name or id, and what is drawn, dimensioned, tagged or noted there is in it

family : {name?, category?: furniture|casework|plumbing|lighting|generic|door|window, parameters?: [{name, kind?: length|number|angle|yesno|material, instance?, value?, formula?}], types?: {type: {parameter: value}}, forms?: [{plane?: xy|xz|yz, profile?: [[a, b], …], circle?: {centre: [a, b], radius}, axis?: [[a, b], [a, b]], from?, to, material?, visible?, void?}], symbols?: [{line?: [[x, y], …] | arc?: {centre: [x, y], radius, from?, to} | text?: {at: [x, y], height, value, align?: left|center|right} | dot?: {centre: [x, y], radius}, visible?}], form?: {id | guid, …a form's fields}, symbol?: {id | guid, …a symbol's fields}, delete_form?: [id | guid, …], delete_symbol?: [id | guid, …], operation?: swing|double-swing|sliding|double-sliding|folding|fixed (a door's or window's, for IFC and schedules), kind?: which fixture or fitting it is, for IFC's predefined type (plumbing: wc|lav|sink|laundry|shower|bath|bidet|urinal; drain: floor_drain|floor_waste|roof_drain; pipefitting: bend|tee|cross|transition|coupling; "" clears it), connectors?: [{kind: power|switch, system: power-balanced|power-unbalanced|switch, poles?: 1-3, voltage?, load_va?, power_factor?, classification?}], rename?, delete?: true, dry_run?, path?, save?} a family of the project's, BIMCraft's own parametric component: created, changed, read, or loaded from the .json file at `path` (a family as `inspect` shows it, with its `name`). Without `name` it lists the project's families, each its category and how many types, forms and symbols it has; with only a `name` it reads one — its definition, each of its types' parameter values worked out, and `warnings` — and changes nothing: no undo step, no file. `dry_run` reads a change the same way and replies what it would do (`changes`: the parameters and types added, taken away and changed, the forms and symbols replaced, patched and deleted by id, the `rename`) instead of doing it; a change that's refused comes back as an error, as it would without it. `form` merges its fields over the one form of that `id` or `guid` (a `null` takes a field away; its place, its id and its GUID stay), `delete_form` takes those forms away; `symbol` and `delete_symbol` do the same for symbols — where `forms` and `symbols` still replace whole lists. Every reply carries `warnings`: what's worth knowing and doesn't stop the change (a void cutting no solid, a form outside the opening or thicker than its wall, a door's or window's plan with no symbols). Its forms are profiles drawn in its own axes (x along a component's angle, y to its left, z up from its base) and swept: `xy` up from `from` to `to`, `xz` along y, `yz` along x. With an `axis`, a line in that plane, the profile is turned about it instead, `from` to `to` degrees (up to 360, right-handed from the axis' first point toward its second; it can't cross the axis): a pipe, a bowl, a lamp shade. A `void` is no solid: it cuts the solid forms listed before it that it passes through, a hole, a notch, a sink's bowl, and is never seen itself (forms listed after it are whole). A `door` or `window` family stands in a wall, placed with `door` or `window` and a `family`: its forms are drawn in the opening's axes (x along the wall from the middle of the opening, y across it, 0 in the middle of the wall and + toward its exterior, z up from the sill), it must have length parameters `Width` and `Height` (the opening it makes; `Sill Height` is a window's default sill), and its formulas read `Wall Thickness`, the wall's. Sizes are mm, or formulas over its parameters as Revit's are: `Width / 2`, `if(Depth > 600, 4, 2)`, with + - * / ^, < > = <= >=, if, and, or, not, min, max, abs, sqrt, round, roundup, rounddown, sin, cos, tan (degrees). A parameter is each type's, or with `instance` each component's. `types` merges into its types (a null takes one away); `parameters` and `forms` replace its own; `material` is a material's name or a material parameter's; `visible` a yes/no parameter or formula. `inspect` lists the families. A device's `connectors` say what it draws: one `power` connector at most (a second is refused), `voltage` in volts, `load_va` in VA (a number or a formula over its parameters, so each type has its load; `power-unbalanced` may take a list, one load for each pole), `power_factor` over 0 up to 1, and its `classification` (`lighting`…); a `switch` connector carries no load. A component reports them as `connectors` in `elements`; a lighting, outlet or switch family without one counts as zero load, which `inspect` warns of; `connectors` replace their own, as `parameters`, `forms` and `symbols` do. The `symbols` of a family of any category are what its plan draws besides its forms, in its own axes, turned and moved (and mirrored) with the component or opening and hidden at coarse detail: each one `line` (points), `arc` (degrees from +x counter-clockwise, up to a full turn), `text` or `dot`, one of them, with `visible` a yes/no parameter or formula. A `text` is lettered in BIMCraft's own strokes, capitals `height` mm tall, `at` the middle of the line of text vertically (`align` says whether `at` is where it starts, its middle or its end); its anchor moves with the component but its letters always read upright, left to right, never turned or mirrored; `{Parameter Name}` in its `value` is replaced by that parameter's value (a name the family lacks is refused), up to 256 characters. A `dot` is a solid disc in ink of a radius above zero. Symbols draw in the plan and ceiling plan of the component's level whatever height it has, and on no other level's. IFC leaves symbols out

component : {family, type?, at: [x,y], level?, angle?, offset?, mirrored?, params?: {parameter: value}} a family's type placed, its first by default: at a point on a level, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise, `offset` mm up from the level, and with `mirrored` flipped across its own x axis; `params` sets its instance parameters (`modify` merges into them, a null taking one back to the family's)

modify : {id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it

delete : {ids: [id,…]} deleting a wall deletes its doors and windows, deleting those their tags; a view takes its notes and spot elevations, and what a spot elevation reads takes it; dimensions lose what's deleted

purge : {kinds?: [type|family|material|picture|filter|template, …], dry_run?} takes out what nothing uses, again for what that leaves unused: types and families unless `kinds` says; a category keeps a type and a family a type; with `dry_run` it lists what would go and changes nothing

schedule : {name?, category?, categories?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?, path?} a schedule view, as Revit's View > Schedules makes one, and its table: columns, rows, the `elements` each row lists, and totals (and a .csv file with a path, or an .xlsx workbook for a path ending .xlsx). A new one needs `name` and `category`: rooms, doors, windows, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, columns, structural columns, footings, beams, strip footings, components, stairs, ramps, railings or levels, or `multicategory`, as Revit's Multi-Category Schedule: a row for each element of `categories` (["walls", "doors"…]; none, every built one but rooms, levels and masses), with the fields they share (Category, Family, Type, Level, Count, Width, Height, Length, Thickness, Area: a wall's length by its height, a door's width by its height; Material: its type's structure layer's, a run's type's, a family's), each empty where its category has none; `category` alone reads its own (Room Schedule, Door Schedule, Window Schedule, Wall Schedule, Floor Schedule, Level Schedule, each the project's once changed). `fields`: its columns, in order, each a field's name (`available` lists them: its category's own, Count, project parameters, a component's family's parameters) or {name, formula?, kind?: number|length|area|yesno, heading?, total?}; with a formula, a calculated field worked out from the row's other fields as a family's formulas are (lengths in mm, areas in m²; `Area * 120`); `total` sums it in a totals row. `filters`: [{field, op: equals|not-equals|greater|greater-or-equal|less|less-or-equal|contains|not-contains|begins-with|not-begins-with|ends-with|not-ends-with|has-value|has-no-value, value}, …], the elements all of them keep (text in any case, numbers as the schedule shows them, an unset yes or no as no). `sort`: [field or {field, descending?}, …], in turn (its first column unless it says; Phase Created and Phase Demolished in the project's order of phases, a phase never demolished after the last); `grouped`, a row for each set of the sort fields' values: Count and totals summed, and a field whose values differ left empty. Each one given replaces the last; `fields: []` goes back to its category's

camera : {eye?: [x, y, z], target?: [x, y, z], lens?: mm, view?: a 3D view's name or id, name?} a 3D camera as Revit's Camera tool makes one: with `eye` (where the camera stands, mm) and `target` (what it looks at, mm) it makes a new named perspective 3D view looking from `eye` at `target` through `lens` (35 mm unless given, 10 to 600), named `name` or by number ("Camera 1", "Camera 2"…). With `view` too, it gives that 3D view the camera instead (its id stays; `{3D}` may be given one): a point left out stays as that camera has it, so `lens` alone or one point alone changes just that, and a view without a camera yet needs both. With `view` and none of `eye`, `target` or `lens` it reads the camera back: `eye`, `target`, `lens` and whether the view is in perspective (null eye/target for a view with no camera yet). The eye is never on the target, so the view always has a direction to look in

library : {kind?, name?} the project's library with its ids and GUIDs, as elements have them: each type (`kind` `type:wall`, `type:door`, `type:beam`…), material, picture, family, parameter, view filter and template (`view-filter`, `view-template`), phase, phase filter, design option set and design option (`option-set`, `design-option`, named `set: option`), family type and family parameter (`family-type`, `family-parameter`, named `family: name`); and `parts`, what entries hold that has its own id and GUID: each type's layers and each family's forms and symbols (`kind` `layer`, `form`, `symbol`; `name` the type's or the family's). Wherever a command takes an entry by name, its GUID does too

elements : {category?, level?, limit?, offset?} elements with their `id` (six digits, what commands take) and `guid` (made once, never changed), fields and derived values (length, height, area_m2…); what an element points at (its level, host, view…) it holds by GUID. Wherever a command takes an element, its id or its GUID will do

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fm.py [-m] -f in.bimcraft cmds.txt: each filter line's reply as `rules -> matches` (or the error)."""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
exe = '/workspace/executable'
a = sys.argv[1:]
if a[0] == '-m':
    exe = os.environ['MINE']; a = a[1:]
infile = a[1]; cmds = a[2]
for l in open(cmds):
    l = l.strip()
    if not l or l.startswith('#'): continue
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=os.environ.get('SCRATCH'))
    shutil.copy(infile, d)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', os.path.basename(infile), '--cmd', l], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    out = p.stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1]
    try:
        r = json.loads(out)
        if 'matches' in r:
            print(json.dumps(r['rules']), '->', r['matches'])
        else:
            print(l[:100], '->', p.stderr.strip()[:200])
    except Exception:
        print(l[:100], '->', p.stderr.strip()[:200])

import subprocess, os, json, sys
mine = os.environ['MINE']
scen = [l.strip() for l in open('/tmp/views-graphics/t/r1.txt') if l.strip()]
os.makedirs('/tmp/views-graphics/rooms', exist_ok=True)
queries = [
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Area","op":"greater","value":%s}]}',
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Area","op":"equals","value":%s}]}',
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Perimeter","op":"equals","value":%s}]}',
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Volume","op":"equals","value":%s}]}',
]
same = tot = 0
for i, l in enumerate(scen):
    cmds = [c for c in l.split(' ;; ') if not c.startswith('schedule')]
    f = '/tmp/views-graphics/rooms/r%d.bimcraft' % i
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    args += ['--cmd', 'schedule {"category":"room","fields":["Name","Area","Perimeter","Volume"]}', '--save', f]
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    rows = None
    for line in p.stdout.split('\n'):
        if '"rows"' in line:
            rows = json.loads(line)['rows']
    if rows is None:
        print('no rows', i, p.stderr[:200]); continue
    for r in rows:
        for q, v in zip(queries, [r[1] - 0.5, r[1], r[2], r[3]]):
            c = q % json.dumps(v)
            o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', f, '--cmd', c], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1]
            mm = subprocess.run([mine, 'run', f, '--cmd', c], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1]
            tot += 1
            if o == mm:
                same += 1
            else:
                print('DIFF', i, c)
                print('   orig', o[:200])

import subprocess, json, math, os
# rooms with a round column of each diameter: find the perimeter the original compares (to the mm)
for d in [100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 800, 1000, 1500]:
    f = '/tmp/views-graphics/s/circ%d.bimcraft' % d
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--cmd', 'wall {"points":[[0,0],[10000,0],[10000,6000],[0,6000]],"closed":true}',
            '--cmd', 'type {"category":"column","name":"R%d","width":%d,"round":true}' % (d, d),
            '--cmd', 'column {"at":[3000,3000],"type":"R%d"}' % d, '--cmd', 'room {"point":[8000,3000]}', '--save', f]
    subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True)
    # bisect the perimeter added
    lo, hi = 32000.0, 32000.0 + math.pi * d + 5
    def gt(v):
        c = 'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Perimeter","op":"greater","value":%s}]}' % v
        o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', f, '--cmd', c], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1]
        return '"matches":[]' not in o
    # integer search: largest integer v with value > v
    a, b = int(lo), int(hi)
    while a < b:
        mid = (a + b + 1) // 2
        if gt(mid):
            a = mid
        else:
            b = mid - 1
    added = a + 1 - 32000
    best = []
    for n in range(6, 200):
        p = 2 * n * (d / 2) * math.sin(math.pi / n)
        if abs(round(32000 + p) - (32000 + added)) < 0.5:
            best.append(n)
    print(d, 'perimeter added ~', added, 'circle', round(math.pi * d, 2), 'n candidates', best[:3], best[-3:] if best else '')

content.text:
The GRAPHICS part is done: `graphics`, `scale`, `detail`, `visual_style`, `filter` and `template` are implemented and committed on branch `worktree-agent-a1b33ce6a0f3d4ac2`, last commit `998bb61`. Against the original, 1485 of 1514 regression probes give identical replies, errors and saved files, and 60+ randomized command sequences matched on every reply and saved file. None of the 29 remaining differences come from my commands. One of them is a real gap that needs a one-line change in `mod.rs` (first item below). The others are commands not built yet (crop, linework, modify, duplicate_view, cad_layers, schedule, section) and `inspect` keys owned by other areas, such as `families`.

**What matches the original, per command**
- **`graphics`**
  - Finding the view: by id, name or GUID; sheets aren't found by number or name; `{3D}` in any case; reading the 3D view doesn't create it, a change does.
  - Error texts and the order in which errors win; the template-control refusal comes first, and a reset skips it.
  - Categories in any case, singular or plural, including subcategories and family categories.
  - hide/show, with rooms and the room reference using `shown`; element overrides; applied filters (up to 32, no duplicates).
  - phase, phase filter and design options (options by name only); CAD layers; background grid patches; `template`; `reset`.
  - Dependent plan views follow their parent. Saved key order and field order inside each view element match.
- **`scale`, `detail`, `visual_style`:** defaults (1 : 96 in feet and inches), the dependent-view and template refusals, and saving (fine and shaded are not stored; a scale is stored even when it is 100).
- **`filter`:** create, update, read and delete (deleting removes it from every view and template); rule parsing and checks per category; library entries; GUID storage for parameter, phase and design-option rules.
- **`template`:** `from`, `like` (only when creating), `kind`, `controls`, `view_range` merge and check, `rename`, `delete`, `reset`, `views`; the rules for when a template gets created; GUIDs accepted for template and filter names.
- **`inspect_entries`** for both sections; undo labels; long errors clipped at 2000 characters. My model check uses the original's wording and order (filters, then templates, then views).

**What doesn't match, or is approximate**
- **`elements` on levels:** `mod.rs::element_view` never sends levels to my code, so a level's graphics show GUIDs where the original shows names.
- **Filter `matches`:** these use my own stand-in for schedule fields and values, since READERS hasn't written schedules yet. That includes a room-boundary calculation for room Area, Perimeter and Volume (wall centre lines or faces, separation lines, columns). It matched every case I tried, but curved walls and unusual layouts aren't verified.
- **Model check order on broken files:** the styles phase check runs before mine, so a file broken in several ways at once may report a different error first.

**What others need to do**
- In `mod.rs::element_view`, add `"level" => graphics::element_view(pr, id, x)`. The plans, sections and 3D-view sub-agents should call `graphics::element_view` from their own `element_view`.
- `delete` and the CAD-drawing owner should call `vg::forget(pr, &guids)` so views drop overrides and hidden layers of deleted elements and drawings. I deliberately don't check those references in the model check; otherwise deleting an element a view overrides would be refused.
- The core's `open` doesn't run the model check; the original refuses invalid files when opening them.

**Functions I expose**
- `graphics::apply(pr, cmd, params)`: for `show_mass` and anything else that edits a view's graphics through the same refusals.
- `graphics::lookup_view`, `label`, `view_reply`, `clip`.
- `vg::effective_of`, `source_of`, `parent_of`, `template_of`, `controls_of`, `gput`: anyone writing graphics keys, `linework` included, should use `gput` to keep the saved order.
- `vg::forget`.
- `templates::view_range_of`, `controlled`, `used`, `delete_template`: `modify` needs `controlled` to refuse a view-range change that a template controls.
- `filters::used`, `delete_filter`, `matches_of` (`used` and the delete functions are for `purge`).

My regression command files are in `/tmp/views-graphics/t/`; `runall.py` and `fuzz.py` in `/tmp/views-graphics/` re-run them.
